items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: I worked in the -- had a job in Philadelphia at a place called the Madhouse. Jake Gillum's Madhouse... So he gave me this job back. Now this is my first organization of having an outfit together that would sound something like a band.

ctx.x: See, before I left, I told you, the last days of '18, before we went in, the beginning of '18, the last days of '17, rather, I worked in the -- had a job in Philadelphia at a place called the Madhouse. Jake Gillum's Madhouse, it was Jessup and Poplar Streets in Philadelphia. Cause I wanted to be home, see. And in being there, so when I went to war, I come out and went back there to see Jake Gillum, and ask him, "Well, I've just been in the war, and could I get my job back." And he said, "Well, sure, anytime a man…
I see. But let's go back, then, because you were at the Madhouse before you went into the service.
